snippet.title: You Can't Tell If I'm Real Anymore. And That's Now YouTube's Problem Too.
snippet.description:
Newsletter: https://natesnewsletter.substack.com/ 
AI voice cloning is already good enough to fool a half-watching audience. The harder problem is that people can no longer tell what was human, what was synthetic, and who is accountable for the final result.

My Links:
👉🏻 X: https://x.com/natebjones
👉🏻 TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@nate.b.jones
👉🏻 Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/nate.b.jones

What's really happening inside the question "was this made with AI?"

The common story says AI content is either a harmless gimmick or an existential threat, but the real question is who stays accountable for the final thing you're watching.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on what "made with AI" really means:

 - Why voice cloning already passes in a half-watching feed
 - How full human presence still breaks in the small details
 - What "made with AI" really splits into five questions
 - Where AI can help and where human judgment has to own the result

AI will keep getting better at polish, so the creators and companies who win will be the ones who stay legibly human, disclose clearly, and keep a real person accountable for what ships.

Every AI model suddenly looks replaceable, and picking the right one has turned into a second job. This video is a practical model picker: how to choose which AI to use for real work without overpaying or drowning in model names.

What's really happening when every AI model suddenly looks replaceable?

The common story is that the smartest model wins. The real question is which intelligence a specific job actually needs.

In this video, I share the inside scoop on how to pick the right AI for the work in front of you:

 - Why daily-driver models differ from cheap workhorse models like GLM 5.2
 - How to route familiar work to cheaper models and review it fast
 - What to keep on a frontier model when the shape of the job is unclear
 - Where specialists win: images, video, live web, and coding harnesses

The models will keep changing, but if you route by the job and keep your context portable, no single model going away can stall your work.

— CHAPTERS:

0:00 Intro: The post-AI world
1:30 Why credentials broke
2:30 Why "keep up with AI" and "just develop taste" are both incomplete
4:00 What the subtle skills actually are (the trustworthiness of desire)
7:30 Where this comes from: Hillman, Buddhism, the daimon
8:30 How to cultivate it: getting at the root of your desire
10:30 A theory of value for the post-AI age

IN CONVERSATION WITH

James Hillman, The Soul's Code (1996). The acorn theory of calling: there's something in you that wants to come forth, and the credentialing system was designed to suppress exactly that.

Daniel Thorson, The End of Hoop Jumping. The hill-climbing vs. valley-crossing frame; the system that manufactured hoop-jumpers; what AI is actually automating.

Rob Burbea, Soulmaking Dharma / Eros Unfettered. Desire as path, not problem. The trustworthiness of eros, properly engaged.

Dan Shipper, AI Creates More Work for Humans, Not Less (Every). The shift from execution to planning and review; why being clear about what good looks like becomes the bottleneck.

Michael Spence, Job Market Signaling (1973). Why credentials worked: they were costly to fake. AI removes the cost.

Randall Collins, The Credential Society (1979). 50 years of credential inflation, and the bureaucratic logic behind it.

Galdin and Silbert, Making Talk Cheap: Generative AI and Labor Market Signaling (2025). When LLMs flatten written applications, the market becomes less meritocratic, not more: top-quintile workers hired 19% less, bottom-quintile 14% more.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08785

Cui, Dias and Ye, Signaling in the Age of AI: Evidence from Cover Letters (2025). Companion empirical study, same direction.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25054

Peter Cappelli (Wharton). On what employers are actually doing when they cite AI for layoffs: "they're just hoping."

Zak Stein. On standardized testing as an instrument of bureaucracy, not a theory of intelligence.

snippet.title: Learn Anything Faster with the S.M.A.R.T. Learning Framework
snippet.description:
1-Page PDF Summary: https://lozeron-academy-llc.kit.com/smart-learning
Productivity Game Academy (includes a 2-week accelerated learning guide): https://tinyurl.com/academyPG

Whether you want to quickly sound knowledgeable at work, ace an exam, or level up a new skill like pickleball, you can do it surprisingly quickly by focusing on five meta-learning skills from the best learning science books.

🔑 The SMART Framework:
1. State Optimization: Learn how to intensely focus before you even start studying. We’ll show you the 15-30 minute trick that floods your brain with focus-enhancing neurochemicals, backed by research in Spark and Deep Work.

2. Mistake Optimization: Discover the "sweet spot" for mistakes: the 85/15 rule. Learn how failing 15% of the time keeps your brain primed for maximum growth, and how to use AI to design perfect practice drills.

3. Active Recall: Stop just reviewing notes! Learn why effort = retention. We'll share three simple habits (Periodic Pause, End-of-session recap, and Start-of-session recall) from Make It Stick that force your brain to build strong neural pathways.

4. Reduction: Complexity fades, simplicity endures. Master the art of reducing everything you learn into one thing: an Acronym, a Sentence, a Page, or a Visual. (Inspired by books like Atomic Habits).

5. Turning Off: The most critical step. Learn why masters prioritize sleep (1.5 hours more than average!) and how naps can boost recall by 20%. True learning and consolidation happen when you rest, as detailed in Why We Sleep and Peak.

Stop studying harder and start studying SMART! Tap the link to subscribe for more science-backed productivity hacks!
